label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 4
knowledgePattern: Propagate ordering restrictions through successive position changes
solution:
Immediately before D drops three positions, D must be first or second. E began ahead of D and none of the earlier moves can put E behind D, so D is second and E is first at this stage.

C began ahead of D. For D now to be ahead of C, C must have crossed D during its one-place drop: D was immediately behind C. They then remain adjacent when A goes to the back. Hence the order before D drops is E, D, C, B, A.

D drops from second to fifth, moving C, B and A forward. The final order is E, C, B, A, D. Answer A.
